verdict.rationale: Slate is documented as a terminal coding agent that takes natural-language prompts (e.g. reviewing the whole codebase and creating ARCH.md) and supports @filename references, multi-hour sessions, parallel subagents and manual integration testing. The community thread describes a one-sentence library port, though critics questioned its scope and verifiability without showing it failed. The docs never explicitly describe implementing a feature or fixing a bug by editing multiple files, so the core is implied rather than documented. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of plain-language feature/bug implementation with multi-file edits, and independent hands-on corroboration of working multi-file changes.
